sentences.text: What happens when a lifetime gamer finally decides to turn off his console and be useful for a single day?
Pure psychological horror.
Step one: touching grass.
Outside air hits my lungs like chemical warfare.
I tried to clean my bedroom.
Turns out, under three years of pizza boxes, there was actually a wooden floor.
Then I tried applying for a real job.
The application asked for five years of experience for an entry-level position.
I attempted to cook real food instead of eating instant ramen.
I managed to set water on fire.
The worst part about real life?
There is no quick-save button.
You drop a plate, and it's gone forever.
I tried talking to a normal human being outside.
We made awkward eye contact for four seconds and I aged ten years.
Nobody warned me that adulting is basically paying a subscription fee just to exist in a server that lags constantly.
After four hours of total productivity, my brain felt like a fried graphics card running Crysis on max settings.
I looked at my life, looked at my chores, and made the only logical executive decision.
I pressed the power button.
The console beeped.
Balance was instantly restored to the universe.
Sure, I'm unemployed, broke, and living in squalor.
But at least my K-D ratio is positive.
Being useful is overrated.
Grinding in a fictional video game simulator is where true fulfillment lies.
Send this to that friend who really needs to touch grass today.
